explanation: Decameron means 'ten days' in Greek: ten storytellers each tell a tale a day for ten days. Chaucer's pilgrims were meant to tell far more than his 24 tales.

claims.text: Chaucer's Canterbury Tales contains 24 tales, some of them unfinished.
The title Decameron comes from Greek words meaning ten days.
In the Decameron, ten storytellers each tell one tale a day for ten days.
In the General Prologue, Chaucer's pilgrims plan to tell far more tales than the 24 he completed.
